The new backend Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host explicitly defaults blank category_id to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, so the server state diverges from the client, which computes category from a null id (undefined), leaving the badge blank until reload. Mechanism is verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: Post-save category state diverges from the server when no category was chosen: for a new host saved without touching the chooser, `categoryId` is null and the backend defaults to uncategorized, but the frontend sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` → undefined, so the row renders with no category badge until reload

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6#save`, the client sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')`, where `categoryId` is initialized to `null` and, for a newly created host (`addHost()` creates a new record), may remain unset. The server (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) explicitly defaults a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, but the success callback then does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`; if `categoryId` is still `null`, this sets `host.category` to `undefined`, so the UI can render without a category badge until reload despite the server having assigned uncategorized.
